mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 7.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a recession and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 7.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 850,000 units and the federal funds rate is below 0.5%, it signals a weak economy with accommodative monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as recession fears intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST < 850 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 420,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS > 420,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 95.0 signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: High employment growth (PAYEMS > 100,000 monthly additions) supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index above 235.0 signals accelerating inflation, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 235.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 235.0) with the federal funds rate below 0.5%, the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the Fed is constrained in rate cuts.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 235.0 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5.
